Sequential execution and conservation therefore do not suffice to recover the selected source method characterization.

findings.source_evidence: Section 1.3 extends one-dimensional high-resolution methods; Section 1.2 requires numerical fluxes that approximate physical fluxes.
findings.translation_evidence: The rule is arbitrary, constant-line consistency depends on an arbitrary admission predicate, and assumed flux-error bounds need not be small.
findings.impact: The translated conclusions do not establish that the sequential updates constitute the source's stated class of constituent methods, even under the coordinator-selected geometry convention.

findings.translation_evidence: Cartesian matching concerns volumes and numerical-rule scaling only. It does not identify actual regions, face measures, or supplied normal fluxes with the Cartesian boxes and independently quantified lifted flux.
findings.impact: Adjudication is needed to determine whether this conditional algebraic specialization satisfies the recorded requirement to retain a measured Cartesian specialization of the same construction.

findings.source_evidence: The introductory splitting description leaves computational domains and analytic stage hypotheses unspecified.
findings.translation_evidence: The theorem uses the full integer lattice and assumes admitted prefix states, reference fields satisfying directional integral conservation, and error bounds at every stage.
findings.impact: The available evidence does not establish that the intended source setting supplies all these assumptions. They cannot be classified as genuine stronger conclusions merely because they permit additional estimates.

findings.source_evidence: The printed paragraph does not define logical rectangularity or precise discontinuity regularity.
findings.translation_evidence: Coordinate connectivity, supplied volumes, and conservative successive updates align with the separately recorded coordinator convention; rectangle conservation aligns with the applicable inherited discontinuity interpretation.
findings.impact: These conventions explain part of the translation but remain separate from printed-source assertions. They do not authorize a requested verdict or erase the original source ambiguity.

rationale: The translation accurately captures chronological coordinate coverage, conservative signs, cell averaging, and several useful conditional identities under the recorded coordinator-selected interpretation. It also preserves integral rather than universally classical solution semantics. Nevertheless, the constituent high-resolution method linkage is missing, and geometric specialization and applicability questions remain unresolved. The inherited user interpretation applies to the identified discontinuity context without supplying broader stage-existence or geometry conventions. Acceptance is therefore withheld and adjudication requested.
